comps.about: Each team plays all six teams in the other group: three Tests in July, three in November.
comps.finals: Finals weekend at Twickenham, 27 to 29 November 2026: each place in the Northern group plays the same place in the Southern group, so 1st v 1st decides the title.
comps.name: Nations Championship

sim.about: We play the rest of the Nations Championship 20,000 times with the model behind every pick in the app: the remaining group Tests, then finals weekend, where England are at home at Twickenham. Ties on points are split by points difference, then points scored.

comps.about: Twelve World Cup qualifiers. Each plays the six teams in the other pool across July and November, and each pool crowns a champion.

comps.about: Canada, New Zealand, Australia and the United States play each other once.
comps.name: Pacific Four Series

comps.about: Touring Tests between the top women’s teams from September to October, with no league table.
comps.name: WXV Global Series

comps.about: The second tier: two pools of three in Hong Kong, each team playing the other pool.
comps.name: WXV Global Series Challenger

m.format: 24 teams in six pools of four. The top two in each pool and the four best third-placed teams reach a new round of 16, then quarter-finals, semi-finals and the final.
m.name: Rugby World Cup 2027

sim.about: We play the whole World Cup 20,000 times using the model behind every pick in the app: each team’s chance of winning a match comes from its World Rugby ranking points, with Australia at home. Scores are drawn from how Tests between ranked teams have gone since 2023, to settle bonus points and points difference. Results replace the simulation as they come in.
